records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֒ אֱמֹ֣ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן נְטֵ֤ה אֶת־יָדְךָ֙ בְּמַטֶּ֔ךָ עַל־הַ֨נְּהָרֹ֔ת עַל־הַיְאֹרִ֖ים וְעַל־הָאֲגַמִּ֑ים וְהַ֥עַל אֶת־הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, say to Aaron, stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up the frogs on [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Hold out your hand with your staff over the rivers, the canals, and the pools, and bring the frogs up over the land of Egypt.'"

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the pools, and bring up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.'"

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Tell Aaron to hold out his staff over the rivers, the canals, and the ponds. He must make the frogs come up onto the land of Egypt."

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text begins chapter 8 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text 7:26-29 are the first four verses of the frog plague, and 8:1-28 follow. Many Bibles number these verses 8:1-4 and 8:5-32, so 8:1 here is 8:5 there, and 8:28 here is 8:32 there.

decisions.choice: rivers, canals, pools: the branches of the Nile, the channels dug from it, and standing water
decisions.reason: The same three words name Egypt's waters in 7:19. "Rivers" are the arms of the Nile in its delta; the "canals" carried its water to the fields.

decisions.choice: the frogs: the plague already announced
decisions.reason: The article points back to the warning given to Pharaoh in 7:27-29, where God said frogs would fill the land, the houses and even the ovens.

records.heading: Frogs cover the land

records.source: וַיֵּ֤ט אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל מֵימֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וַתַּ֨עַל֙ הַצְּפַרְדֵּ֔עַ וַתְּכַ֖ס אֶת־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And stretched out Aaron his hand over [the] waters of Egypt, and came up the frog[s] and covered [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: So Aaron held his hand out over the waters of Egypt. The frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

L.2: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

R.2: So Aaron held out his hand over the water in Egypt. Frogs came up and covered the land.

decisions.choice: the frog: a singular word for a mass of frogs
decisions.reason: The noun is singular here but means all the frogs together, as "the swarm" does in verses 17-27.

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֥ן הַֽחֲרְטֻמִּ֖ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֶת־הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And did thus the magicians by their enchantments, and brought up the frogs on [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: The magicians matched this with their spells and brought frogs up onto the land of Egypt as well.

L.3: And the magicians did thus by their enchantments, and brought up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.

R.3: But the magicians used their magic and did the same thing. They also made frogs come up onto the land of Egypt.

decisions.choice: magicians: Egyptian priests skilled in sacred writings and magic
decisions.reason: The word is used of the experts at Pharaoh's court in Genesis 41:8 and Exodus 7:11, 22. They can bring up more frogs, but they cannot take any away; Pharaoh has to ask Moses (verse 4).

decisions.choice: enchantments: hidden practices, spells
decisions.reason: The word is related to one meaning "secret" or "quietly". It is the same as in 7:22; a similar word is used in 7:11.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֜ה לְמֹשֶׁ֣ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַעְתִּ֣ירוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְיָסֵר֙ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִמֶּ֖נִּי וּמֵֽעַמִּ֑י וַאֲשַׁלְּחָה֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְיִזְבְּח֖וּ לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And summoned Pharaoh Moses and Aaron and said, entreat Yahweh that he may remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will let go the people that they may sacrifice to Yahweh.
pieces: Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said, "Plead with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to rid me and my people of the frogs, and I will release the people so they can offer sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.4: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, "Entreat {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will let the people go, that they may sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.4: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron. He said, "Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to take the frogs away from me and my people. Then I will let the people go and offer sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: entreat: pray earnestly on someone's behalf
decisions.reason: The verb means to plead with God in prayer. It recurs through the plagues (verses 5, 24-26; 9:28; 10:17-18).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh names Yahweh
decisions.reason: In 5:2 Pharaoh said, "I do not know Yahweh." Now he asks for prayer to Yahweh and promises to let the people go.

decisions.choice: entreat / plead with / pray
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word, "entreat", for this verb throughout the chapter. Balanced and Readable use the everyday words.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה לְפַרְעֹה֮ הִתְפָּאֵ֣ר עָלַי֒ לְמָתַ֣י׀אַעְתִּ֣יר לְךָ֗ וְלַעֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ וּֽלְעַמְּךָ֔ לְהַכְרִית֙ הַֽצֲפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִמְּךָ֖ וּמִבָּתֶּ֑יךָ רַ֥ק בַּיְאֹ֖ר תִּשָּׁאַֽרְנָה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Pharaoh, glorify yourself over me: for when shall I entreat for you and for your servants and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses? Only in the River will they remain.
pieces: Moses said to Pharaoh, "The choice is yours, and the honor: say when I should pray for you, your officials, and your people, and the frogs will be cut off from you and your houses. They will stay only in the Nile."

L.5: And Moses said to Pharaoh, "Have the honor over me: for when shall I entreat for you and for your servants and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses? Only in the Nile will they remain."

R.5: Moses said to Pharaoh, "You may choose the time. Tell me when I should pray for you, your officials, and your people. Then the frogs will be taken away from you and your houses. The only frogs left will be the ones in the Nile River."

decisions.choice: glorify yourself over me: you may have the honor of setting the time
decisions.reason: The phrase is found only here. It seems to be a courteous formula: Moses gives Pharaoh the advantage of naming the time, so that when the frogs go at that time the work is plainly God's (verse 6). Others take it as a challenge, "boast over me". The Septuagint has "appoint for me when I should pray".

decisions.choice: the River: the Nile
decisions.reason: The word is the Egyptian name for the Nile, used of it throughout 7:15-25.

decisions.choice: your officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his court and officials (5:21). Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְמָחָ֑ר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כִּדְבָ֣רְךָ֔ לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּי־אֵ֖ין כַּיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said, tomorrow. And he said, according to your word, so that you may know that there is none like Yahweh our God.
pieces: Pharaoh answered, "Tomorrow." Moses said, "Then it will be done at your word, and you will learn that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has no equal.

L.6: And he said, "Tomorrow." And he said, "[Let it be] according to your word, so that you may know that there is none like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

R.6: Pharaoh said, "Tomorrow." Moses said, "It will happen just as you have said. Then you will know that no one is like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

decisions.choice: there is none like Yahweh our God: he has no equal
decisions.reason: The plagues answer Pharaoh's question "Who is Yahweh?" (5:2). The same claim is made in 9:14 and sung in 15:11.

decisions.choice: according to your word: as you have said
decisions.reason: Moses accepts the time Pharaoh named.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh ... Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "he said ... he said". Balanced and Readable name the speakers; Literal keeps "he".

records.source: וְסָר֣וּ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֗ים מִמְּךָ֙ וּמִבָּ֣תֶּ֔יךָ וּמֵעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וּמֵעַמֶּ֑ךָ רַ֥ק בַּיְאֹ֖ר תִּשָּׁאַֽרְנָה׃
records.gloss: And will depart the frogs from you and from your houses and from your servants and from your people; only in the River will they remain.
pieces: The frogs will go away from you, from your houses, from your officials, and from your people. Only in the Nile will any be left."

L.7: And the frogs will depart from you and from your houses and from your servants and from your people; only in the Nile will they remain."

R.7: The frogs will go away from you and your houses. They will go away from your officials and your people. The only frogs left will be in the Nile."

decisions.choice: depart: turn aside, go away
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Pharaoh used in verse 4, "remove". It is used again of the flies in verses 25 and 27.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן מֵעִ֣ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה עַל־דְּבַ֥ר הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֥ם לְפַרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And went out Moses and Aaron from with Pharaoh, and cried out Moses to Yahweh concerning [the] matter of the frogs which he had set for Pharaoh.
pieces: Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh's presence, and Moses called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} about the frogs that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sent against Pharaoh.

L.8: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning the matter of the frogs that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had brought upon Pharaoh.

R.8: Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh. Then Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} about the frogs {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had sent on Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: which he had set for Pharaoh: the frogs that God had brought on Pharaoh
alternatives: as Moses had agreed with Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The subject of "set" is not named. It is most likely God, who sent the frogs. It may instead be Moses: "as he had agreed with Pharaoh", that is, about the time they had set (verses 5-6).

decisions.choice: cried out: called aloud for help
decisions.reason: The verb is used of an urgent cry for help, as of the foremen in 5:15.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהוָ֖ה כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיָּמֻ֨תוּ֙ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִן־הַבָּתִּ֥ים מִן־הַחֲצֵרֹ֖ת וּמִן־הַשָּׂדֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And did Yahweh according to [the] word of Moses, and died the frogs from the houses, from the courtyards, and from the fields.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} granted Moses' request. In the houses, the courtyards, and the fields, the frogs died off.

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did according to the word of Moses, and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courtyards, and out of the fields.

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Moses what he asked for. All the frogs died, in the houses, in the yards, and out in the fields.

decisions.choice: courtyards: enclosed yards beside houses
decisions.reason: The word can mean a courtyard or a small settlement, a village. Between "houses" and "fields" it most likely means yards.

decisions.choice: died from the houses: died and were gone from them
decisions.reason: The verb "died" is joined with "from": the frogs died and so were cleared out of each place.

records.source: וַיִּצְבְּר֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם חֳמָרִ֣ם חֳמָרִ֑ם וַתִּבְאַ֖שׁ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And they piled them up heaps, heaps, and stank the land.
pieces: People gathered them into great heaps, and the land stank.

L.10: And they piled them up in heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.

R.10: People piled up the dead frogs in big heaps. The land smelled terrible.

decisions.choice: heaps, heaps: heap after heap
decisions.reason: Repeating the noun shows a great number.

decisions.choice: stank: the same verb as the stinking Nile
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the Nile in 7:18, 21 and of the foremen's complaint in 5:21. The first two plagues both end with a stench in the land.

records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא פַּרְעֹ֗ה כִּ֤י הָֽיְתָה֙ הָֽרְוָחָ֔ה וְהַכְבֵּד֙ אֶת־לִבּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And saw Pharaoh that there was the relief, and he made heavy his heart, and did not listen to them, just as had said Yahweh.
pieces: Once Pharaoh saw that he had breathing room, he hardened his heart. He would not listen to them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

L.11: And Pharaoh saw that there was relief, and he made his heart heavy and did not listen to them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

R.11: But when Pharaoh saw that the frogs were gone, he made himself stubborn. He would not listen to Moses and Aaron. This was just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen.

decisions.choice: relief: breathing space, a respite
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning room or breath. The pressure on Pharaoh was gone.

decisions.choice: he made his heart heavy: Pharaoh himself hardened his heart
decisions.reason: Here Pharaoh is the subject. The verb is from the root "heavy", the one used when Pharaoh made the labor heavy (5:9). God had said Pharaoh would not listen (7:3-4; see 4:21). He goes back on his promise of verse 4.

decisions.choice: hardened his heart / made himself stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "made his heart heavy" to show the Hebrew verb, which differs from "strong" in verse 15. Balanced says "hardened", Readable "stubborn".

decisions.choice: the frogs were gone
decisions.reason: Readable says what the relief was.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֒ אֱמֹר֙ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן נְטֵ֣ה אֶֽת־מַטְּךָ֔ וְהַ֖ךְ אֶת־עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהָיָ֥ה לְכִנִּ֖ם בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, say to Aaron, stretch out your staff and strike [the] dust of the earth, and it will become gnats in all [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Tell Aaron to hold out his staff and strike the dust on the ground. Throughout the land of Egypt the dust will turn into gnats."

L.12: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth,' and it will become gnats in all the land of Egypt."

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Tell Aaron to hold out his staff and hit the dust on the ground. All over Egypt the dust will turn into gnats."

decisions.choice: gnats: small biting insects
decisions.reason: The word is found only in this plague and in Psalm 105:31, so the insect is not certain. It may be gnats, mosquitoes, sand flies or lice; some older translations have "lice". The Septuagint uses a word for gnats or mosquitoes.

records.heading: Gnats

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֗ן וַיֵּט֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־יָד֤וֹ בְמַטֵּ֨הוּ֙ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ וַתְּהִי֙ הַכִּנָּ֔ם בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה כָּל־עֲפַ֥ר הָאָ֛רֶץ הָיָ֥ה כִנִּ֖ים בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And they did so; and stretched out Aaron his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, and there were the gnats on man and on beast; all [the] dust of the earth became gnats in all [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: So they did it. When Aaron raised his staff in his hand and struck the dust of the ground, gnats were on people and animals alike. Across the whole land of Egypt, all the dust turned into gnats.

L.13: And they did so: Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, and the gnats were on humans and on animals; all the dust of the earth became gnats in all the land of Egypt.

R.13: They did it. Aaron held out his staff and hit the dust. Then there were gnats on the people and the animals. All the dust in the land of Egypt turned into gnats.

decisions.choice: all the dust of the earth became gnats: the gnats were everywhere
decisions.reason: A sweeping way of saying how widespread the plague was.

decisions.choice: man and beast: people and animals
decisions.reason: The pair means every living creature, human or animal (9:9-10).

records.source: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֨ן הַחַרְטֻמִּ֧ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֛ם לְהוֹצִ֥יא אֶת־הַכִּנִּ֖ים וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ וַתְּהִי֙ הַכִּנָּ֔ם בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And did thus the magicians by their enchantments to bring forth the gnats, and they were not able; and there were the gnats on man and on beast.
pieces: The magicians attempted the same with their spells, to bring out gnats, but they failed. And still the gnats were on people and animals.

L.14: And the magicians did thus by their enchantments to bring out the gnats, but they were not able. And the gnats were on humans and on animals.

R.14: The magicians tried to use their magic to make gnats too. But they could not do it. And the gnats were still on the people and the animals.

decisions.choice: did so to bring out: tried to bring out
decisions.reason: The magicians set about doing the same, but the attempt failed. It is the first time they cannot copy a sign (7:11, 22; 8:3).

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּים֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֶצְבַּ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִ֑וא וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק לֵב־פַּרְעֹה֙ וְלֹֽא־שָׁמַ֣ע אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And said the magicians to Pharaoh, [the] finger of God [is] it; and was strong [the] heart of Pharaoh, and he did not listen to them, just as had said Yahweh.
pieces: The magicians told Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God at work!" But Pharaoh's heart stayed stubborn, and he refused to listen to them, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

L.15: And the magicians said to Pharaoh, "It [is the] finger of God!" But the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not listen to them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

R.15: The magicians said to Pharaoh, "God has done this!" But Pharaoh was still stubborn. He would not listen to them. This was just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen.

decisions.choice: the finger of God: God's own power at work
decisions.reason: The finger stands for a direct act of God. God writes the tablets with his finger (31:18), and the heavens are the work of his fingers (Psalm 8:4). Jesus uses the phrase of his own works (Luke 11:20).

decisions.choice: God: the magicians do not name Yahweh
decisions.reason: They use the general word for God, which can also mean "a god". They admit a divine power that their arts cannot match.

decisions.choice: the heart was strong: Pharaoh's will stayed firm against God
decisions.reason: This is the verb of 4:21 and 7:13, 22, "be strong", not "heavy" as in verse 11.

decisions.choice: stayed stubborn / was still stubborn
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "was strong"; Balanced and Readable say what a strong heart means here.

decisions.choice: God has done this
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's finger.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הַשְׁכֵּ֤ם בַּבֹּ֨קֶר֙ וְהִתְיַצֵּב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה הִנֵּ֖ה יוֹצֵ֣א הַמָּ֑יְמָה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁלַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh; look, he goes out to the water; and you will say to him, thus says Yahweh, let go my people that they may serve me.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Be up early in the morning and take your stand in front of Pharaoh as he comes out to the water. Say to him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Release {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people so that they can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.16: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and station yourself before Pharaoh. Look, he is going out to the water. And say to him, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, that they may serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning. Go and stand in front of Pharaoh when he goes out to the river. Tell him, 'Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go so they can worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: he goes out to the water: the same meeting place as in 7:15
decisions.reason: Moses is again to meet Pharaoh at the Nile in the morning.

decisions.choice: serve: work for, worship
decisions.reason: The verb means both to work for a master and to worship. It is the word for Israel's forced labor in 1:13-14. Israel is to be released from serving Pharaoh to serve God.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in 7:16, Readable uses "worship", the sense of "serve" that fits a journey to sacrifice; Literal and Balanced keep "serve".

records.heading: Swarms of flies

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־אֵינְךָ֮ מְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ אֶת־עַמִּי֒ הִנְנִי֩ מַשְׁלִ֨יחַ בְּךָ֜ וּבַעֲבָדֶ֧יךָ וּֽבְעַמְּךָ֛ וּבְבָתֶּ֖יךָ אֶת־הֶעָרֹ֑ב וּמָ֨לְא֜וּ בָּתֵּ֤י מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָרֹ֔ב וְגַ֥ם הָאֲדָמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: For if you are not letting go my people, look, I am sending on you and on your servants and on your people and into your houses the swarm; and will be full [the] houses of Egypt [of] the swarm, and also the ground on which they [are].
pieces: If you do not let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, I will send swarms of flies against you, your officials, your people, and your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be filled with the swarms, and so will the very ground where they live.

L.17: For if you do not let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, look, I am sending the swarm upon you and upon your servants and upon your people and into your houses; and the houses of Egypt will be full of the swarm, and also the ground on which they [are].

R.17: If you will not let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, I will send swarms of flies on you, your officials, and your people. They will get into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be full of flies. There will be flies all over the ground too.

decisions.choice: the swarm: swarms of flies or other insects
decisions.reason: The word is found only for this plague (Psalm 78:45; 105:31), and the creature is uncertain. The Septuagint has "dog-fly", a biting fly. The word looks related to a verb for mixing, and a Jewish tradition took it as a mixture of wild animals.

decisions.choice: they: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Even the ground the Egyptians live on will be full of the swarm.

decisions.choice: swarms of flies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the most likely insect; Literal keeps "the swarm".

records.source: וְהִפְלֵיתִי֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֗שֶׁן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עַמִּי֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עָלֶ֔יהָ לְבִלְתִּ֥י הֱיֽוֹת־שָׁ֖ם עָרֹ֑ב לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I will set apart on that day [the] land of Goshen, on which my people [are] standing, so that not to be there [a] swarm, so that you may know that I [am] Yahweh in [the] midst of the land.
pieces: On that day, though, I will set apart Goshen, the region where {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people live: no flies will swarm there. That way you will learn that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am right here in the land.

L.18: And on that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, on which {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people dwell, so that no swarm will be there, so that you may know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the midst of the land.

R.18: But on that day the land of Goshen, where {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people live, will be different. I will not let any flies go there. Then you will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, am right here in this land.

decisions.choice: set apart: treat as different, make a distinction
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something distinct or wonderful. The same verb is used in 9:4 and 11:7, where God distinguishes Israel from Egypt.

decisions.choice: Goshen: the region where Israel lived
decisions.reason: Jacob's family settled in Goshen, in the eastern part of the Nile Delta (Genesis 45:10; 47:27).

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh in the midst of the land: Yahweh is present and at work in Egypt itself
alternatives: in the midst of the earth
decisions.reason: The words can be read "I, Yahweh, am in the midst of the land" or "I am Yahweh, in the midst of the land". Either way the God of the Hebrews acts within Pharaoh's own land. "The land" may also mean the whole earth (9:29).

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י פְדֻ֔ת בֵּ֥ין עַמִּ֖י וּבֵ֣ין עַמֶּ֑ךָ לְמָחָ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה הָאֹ֥ת הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will put [a] redemption between my people and between your people; tomorrow will be this sign.
pieces: I will make a rescue that sets {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people apart from your people. Tomorrow the sign will come.'"

L.19: And I will put a redemption between {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people and your people. Tomorrow this sign will happen.'"

R.19: I will rescue {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and that will set them apart from your people. This sign will come tomorrow.'"

decisions.choice: redemption: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "redemption" or "ransom": God's rescue of his people is what will divide them from the Egyptians. The Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate have "division", which may reflect a Hebrew word differing by one letter and related to the verb "set apart" in verse 18. This translation follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: a rescue that sets my people apart / I will rescue my people
decisions.reason: "Put a redemption between" is not natural English. Balanced and Readable say what it means: God's rescue makes the difference between the two peoples.

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יְהוָה֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹא֙ עָרֹ֣ב כָּבֵ֔ד בֵּ֥יתָה פַרְעֹ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית עֲבָדָ֑יו וּבְכָל־אֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם תִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפְּנֵ֥י הֶעָרֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And did Yahweh so; and came [a] heavy swarm [into the] house of Pharaoh and [the] house of his servants, and in all [the] land of Egypt was ruined the land because of the swarm.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} carried this out. Great swarms of flies invaded Pharaoh's house and his officials' houses. Across the whole land of Egypt, the flies brought ruin to the land.

L.20: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did so; and a heavy swarm came into the house of Pharaoh and the house of his servants, and in all the land of Egypt the land was ruined because of the swarm.

R.20: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} did what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said. Huge swarms of flies came into Pharaoh's palace and into the homes of his officials. The flies ruined the whole land of Egypt.

decisions.choice: heavy: dense, massive
decisions.reason: The adjective is from the root "heavy", the one used of Pharaoh making his heart heavy (verses 11, 28).

decisions.choice: was ruined: was spoiled, destroyed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the earth being corrupted in Genesis 6:11-12.

decisions.choice: what he had said
decisions.reason: Readable says what "did so" refers to: the warning of verses 16-19.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֣א פַרְעֹ֔ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֖ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכ֛וּ זִבְח֥וּ לֵֽאלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And summoned Pharaoh Moses and Aaron and said, go, sacrifice to your God in the land.
pieces: Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said, "Go and offer sacrifices to your God, but do it here in this land."

L.21: And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God in the land."

R.21: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron. He said, "Go and offer sacrifices to your God. But do it here in Egypt."

decisions.choice: in the land: within Egypt
decisions.reason: Pharaoh allows the sacrifice but not the journey into the wilderness (3:18; 5:3). It is the first of several partial offers (8:24; 10:11, 24).

decisions.choice: here in Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says which land is meant.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה לֹ֤א נָכוֹן֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֔ן כִּ֚י תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מִצְרַ֔יִם נִזְבַּ֖ח לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ הֵ֣ן נִזְבַּ֞ח אֶת־תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת מִצְרַ֛יִם לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א יִסְקְלֻֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, not right to do so, for [the] abomination of Egypt we will sacrifice to Yahweh our God; look, we sacrifice [the] abomination of Egypt before their eyes, and will they not stone us?
pieces: Moses answered, "It would not be fitting to do that. The sacrifices we offer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God are offensive to the Egyptians. If we offered, right in front of them, sacrifices they find offensive, they would stone us, would they not?

L.22: And Moses said, "It is not right to do so, for [what is] the abomination of Egypt we will sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. If we sacrifice the abomination of Egypt before their eyes, will they not stone us?

R.22: Moses said, "That would not be right. The Egyptians would be disgusted by the animals we sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. If we offered those sacrifices where they could see us, they would throw stones at us to kill us!

decisions.choice: the abomination of Egypt: what the Egyptians found repugnant
decisions.reason: The same word is used of what Egyptians would not do: eat with Hebrews (Genesis 43:32) or accept shepherds (Genesis 46:34). Certain animals were sacred in Egyptian religion, and seeing them killed in sacrifice could provoke the crowd. The phrase may instead mean "what the Egyptians worship", offered as a sacrifice.

decisions.choice: look: here introducing a condition, "if"
decisions.reason: The word usually means "look", but here it sets up a supposed case, as it can in later Hebrew and Aramaic.

decisions.choice: stone us: kill us by throwing stones
decisions.reason: Stoning was a way a crowd or community put someone to death.

decisions.choice: the animals we sacrifice
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sacrifices were. It turns the question "will they not stone us?" into a statement and explains stoning.

records.source: דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים נֵלֵ֖ךְ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְזָבַ֨חְנוּ֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יֹאמַ֥ר אֵלֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: [A] journey of three days we will go into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to Yahweh our God, just as he says to us.
pieces: We will travel for three days into the wilderness, and there we will sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} instructs us."

L.23: A journey of three days we will go into the wilderness and sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tells us."

R.23: We will go on a three-day trip into the desert. There we will offer sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tells us to do."

decisions.choice: a journey of three days: the request God gave in 3:18
decisions.reason: Moses repeats the request first made in 5:3.

decisions.choice: as he says to us: as he tells us, or will tell us
decisions.reason: The verb form can refer to the present or the future. In 10:26 Moses says they will not know how to worship until they arrive.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֗ה אָנֹכִ֞י אֲשַׁלַּ֤ח אֶתְכֶם֙ וּזְבַחְתֶּ֞ם לַיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר רַ֛ק הַרְחֵ֥ק לֹא־תַרְחִ֖יקוּ לָלֶ֑כֶת הַעְתִּ֖ירוּ בַּעֲדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Pharaoh, I, I will let you go, and you will sacrifice to Yahweh your God in the wilderness; only far you must not go far, to go. Entreat for me.
pieces: Pharaoh said, "Very well, I will release you, and you may sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in the wilderness. Just do not travel too far away. And pray on my behalf."

L.24: And Pharaoh said, "I will let you go, and you shall sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in the wilderness; only you must certainly not go far away. Entreat for me."

R.24: Pharaoh said, "All right. I will let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. But you must not go very far away. And you must pray for me."

decisions.choice: I: emphatic
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: Pharaoh presents the release as his own grant.

decisions.choice: far you must not go far: you must not go far at all
decisions.reason: The doubled verb makes the limit strong.

decisions.choice: entreat for me: pray for me
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 4. Pharaoh again asks for prayer.

decisions.choice: Very well / All right
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show Pharaoh's stressed "I" as a grudging permission.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤א מֵֽעִמָּךְ֙ וְהַעְתַּרְתִּ֣י אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְסָ֣ר הֶעָרֹ֗ב מִפַּרְעֹ֛ה מֵעֲבָדָ֥יו וּמֵעַמּ֖וֹ מָחָ֑ר רַ֗ק אַל־יֹסֵ֤ף פַּרְעֹה֙ הָתֵ֔ל לְבִלְתִּי֙ שַׁלַּ֣ח אֶת־הָעָ֔ם לִזְבֹּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, look, I [am] going out from with you, and I will entreat Yahweh, and will turn aside the swarm from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people tomorrow; only let not Pharaoh again deceive by not letting go the people to sacrifice to Yahweh.
pieces: Moses said, "I am leaving you now, and I will plead with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Tomorrow the flies will depart from Pharaoh, from his officials, and from his people. But Pharaoh must not trick us again and keep the people from going to sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.25: And Moses said, "Look, I am going out from you, and I will entreat {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the swarm will depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people tomorrow. Only let Pharaoh not again deal deceitfully by not letting the people go to sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.25: Moses said, "I am going out now, and I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Tomorrow the flies will leave you, your officials, and your people. But you must not trick us again, Pharaoh! You must let the people go to offer sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: Pharaoh ... Pharaoh: the king spoken of in the third person
decisions.reason: Speaking to a king, Moses names him rather than saying "you", a form of court courtesy.

decisions.choice: deceive: deal falsely, trifle with
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Laban cheating Jacob (Genesis 31:7). Pharaoh promised in verse 4 and went back on it in verse 11.

decisions.choice: you ... Pharaoh!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the courtly third person into "you", since it is plainly Pharaoh who is addressed.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֥א מֹשֶׁ֖ה מֵעִ֣ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיֶּעְתַּ֖ר אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And went out Moses from with Pharaoh and entreated Yahweh.
pieces: Moses went out from Pharaoh's presence and prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.26: And Moses went out from Pharaoh and entreated {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.26: Moses went away from Pharaoh. He prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: entreated: prayed for Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The verb of verses 4-5 and 24-25. Moses prays as Pharaoh asked.

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יְהוָה֙ כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיָּ֨סַר֙ הֶעָרֹ֔ב מִפַּרְעֹ֖ה מֵעֲבָדָ֣יו וּמֵעַמּ֑וֹ לֹ֥א נִשְׁאַ֖ר אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And did Yahweh according to [the] word of Moses, and he removed the swarm from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; not remained one.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses' request and took the flies away from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. Not a single one was left.

L.27: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did according to the word of Moses, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} removed the swarm from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; not one remained.

R.27: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses' prayer. He took all the flies away from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. Not even one fly was left.

decisions.choice: not one remained: the swarm was removed entirely
decisions.reason: Unlike the frogs, some of which stayed in the Nile (verses 5, 7), nothing of the swarm was left.

records.source: וַיַּכְבֵּ֤ד פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶת־לִבּ֔וֹ גַּ֖ם בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֑את וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־הָעָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And made heavy Pharaoh his heart also at this time, and he did not let go the people.
pieces: Yet once again Pharaoh hardened his heart; he did not release the people.

L.28: And Pharaoh made his heart heavy this time also, and he did not let the people go.

R.28: But Pharaoh made himself stubborn again. He still did not let the people go.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh made his heart heavy: again by his own choice
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Pharaoh is the subject of "made heavy", the root used of the heavy swarm (verse 20) and the heavy labor (5:9). His promise of verse 24 is broken, as Moses warned (verse 25).

decisions.choice: hardened his heart / made himself stubborn
decisions.reason: As in verse 11. Literal keeps "made his heart heavy".
